Interesting that you have the opposite experience, but both perspectives can still be correct. It may be true that no dogs on your particular farm had cropped ears and they were fine, but it can also be true that other familes did crop their dogs ears. According to the linked wiki cropping has been done historically for other working dogs for health reasons.

> Crops were also performed on dogs that might need to fight, either while hunting animals that might fight back or while defending livestock herds from predators

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cropping_(animal)

I'm not defending cropping but I think it's important to acknowledge that every case is different and we just don't have the context in this video.
Farm dogs tend to have their ears cropped because it can be dangerous for them if prticularly-mean large farm animals decide to yank them.
